claim: For any Borel probability measure \(\rho\) on \((0,\tfrac12)\), let \(V\sim\rho\) and let \(Z,\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\ldots\) be mutually independent standard normal variables, independent of \(V\), and set \(X_i=\frac{\sqrt{1-2V}}{2}Z+\sqrt V\,\varepsilon_i\). Then \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) is infinitely exchangeable and \(X_i+X_j\sim N(0,1)\) for every \(i\ne j\), regardless of \(\rho\); its covariance matrix depends on \(\rho\) only through \(\mathbb EV\), while the characteristic function of \(X_i-X_j\) is \(\int e^{-vt^2}\rho(dv)\), which uniquely identifies \(\rho\). If \(\rho\) is nondegenerate, the process is not Gaussian because its marginal fourth cumulant is \(3\operatorname{Var}(V)/4>0\). In particular, \(\rho_1=\delta_{1/4}\) and \(\rho_2=\tfrac12\delta_{1/8}+\tfrac12\delta_{3/8}\) yield the same Gaussian pair-sum law and identical covariance matrices, but respectively a Gaussian and a non-Gaussian exchangeable process.
scientific_integrity: The Gaussian sum law and covariance identities are proved analytically. Exact rational arithmetic checks the explicit comparison only. General non-identifiability of exchangeable sequences from partial sums is prior literature and is not claimed as new. Independent audit has not been performed.
scientific_limitations: The result is an explicit family, not a classification of all exchangeable sequences with Gaussian pair sums.
For nondegenerate rho, the one-dimensional marginal is non-Gaussian; no claim is made about examples with Gaussian marginals.
Only the marginal law of each individual pair sum is fixed, not the joint law of the entire array of pair sums.
The difference-law identification applies within this constructed family, not to arbitrary directing measures.
title: Gaussian pair sums hide exchangeable variance mixtures
